title: Substrate Card -- CLAUDE.md Rule 28, THE SUBSTRATE TEST
description: The machine-checkable deliverable of a Rule 28 qualification. Seven questions over three DECLARED grains (PROCESS / ARTIFACT / TRUST). Every row carries its own BASIS, EVIDENCE and OWNER, because Rule 24(iv): the values do not move together and neither do their remedies. Shape follows a document-envelope pattern -- a governed document declares how it came to exist, what it claims temporally, where it lives, and what it is a projection of -- extended with the TRUST grain, which describes whether the thing can be STOOD ON rather than merely what it is.

carded_by.description: Seat serial that produced this card.

kind.description: What class of thing the subject is.

x-rule24.intent: route the reader to the right expectations for the rows below
x-rule24.mece: 'other' closes the population honestly rather than forcing a fit; a value is added only by a naming act
x-rule24.state_coherence: kind is stable for the life of the resource; a change of kind is a new resource

declared_domain.description: What this resource claims to cover. Rule 24(i) requires the domain be NAMED before coverage can be judged.

as_of.description: CONSISTENT STATE IS NOT OPTIONAL. Cards taken at different vintages are individually correct and jointly meaningless -- a wave declares ONE as_of and every card in it carries that stamp. Measured 2026-08-26: a projection lagged its warehouse by 6,261 nodes, and a two-vintage read rendered as a finding about the estate.

carded_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC, from the clock, never estimated.

graph_vintage.description: Snapshot id of the graph read, or null with a stated reason if the subject has no graph dependency.

process.description: GRAIN 1 -- how the resource comes to exist.

how.description: How the resource is defined/assembled, in one paragraph.

determinism.description: Whether re-running produces the same answer.

x-enum-definitions.deterministic: Same inputs always produce the same output. Re-running is a control.
x-enum-definitions.inferential: Produced by a model or other non-deterministic process. Re-running may differ; failure presents as a PLAUSIBLE WRONG OUTPUT rather than an error.
x-enum-definitions.hybrid: A declared deterministic core with named inferential stages; the split MUST be enumerated in inference_detail.
x-enum-definitions.unknown: Not yet determined. An HONEST value -- never default to 'deterministic' because it looks that way.

x-rule24.domain: reproducibility of the process that produces this resource
x-rule24.intent: tell a consumer whether re-running is a control or a coin flip
x-rule24.mece: deterministic / inferential / hybrid partition the reproducibility axis; 'unknown' covers the not-yet-measured member so absence is never rendered as determinism
x-rule24.state_coherence: unknown may resolve to any of the other three; deterministic <-> inferential is a real change to the resource, not a re-reading

inference_detail.description: REQUIRED when determinism is inferential or hybrid. Nested model use is tracked because it prices the system as well as qualifying it.

failure_is_loud.description: false means a failed inference returns plausible content rather than an error -- the dangerous case.

composes.description: What it reuses. Empty array is a claim, not a gap.

invents.description: What it originates. A resource that INVENTS what it should COMPOSE is a duplicate waiting to diverge.

declared_rhythm.description: e.g. 'nightly 02:00Z'. NULL IS A REAL AND COMMON ANSWER -- a resource with no cadence never refreshes on a schedule, which is a defect and not a config gap.

actual_trigger.description: What actually fires it. A resource whose only trigger is another process's success HAS NO SCHEDULE and freezes silently when its upstream breaks.

live_matches_declared.description: DESIRED vs APPLIED. A declared cadence is not evidence the live instance is fresh.

live_instance_age.description: Measured age of the current instance, if read.

artifact.description: GRAIN 2 -- what the resource leaves behind.

persisted.description: FALSE IS A COMMON AND IMPORTANT ANSWER. A resource that persists nothing has no vintage of its own and inherits the freshness of substrates it does not control.

x-enum-definitions.projection: Rebuildable view derived from governed inputs. MUST name projection_of.
x-enum-definitions.evidence: An observation or receipt supporting a claim without becoming source configuration.
x-enum-definitions.reference: External identity or context that informs without governing.
x-enum-definitions.none: Persists nothing; the row exists to say so.

x-rule24.domain: standing of the persisted artifact relative to truth
x-rule24.intent: tell a consumer whether editing this changes the world or gets overwritten
x-rule24.mece: 'none' covers the unpersisted member, which the other four cannot express
x-rule24.state_coherence: a projection promoted to source is a governance act, not a refresh

form.description: e.g. 'Iceberg table', 'JSON on disk', 'in-memory lru_cache only'.

home.description: EXACT location. 'Iceberg/Nessie table X', 's3://bucket/prefix', a repo path, or NULL meaning NOWHERE.

projection_of.description: THE GRAPH-OBJECT LINEAGE. What this artifact is derived FROM. A projection that cannot name its source cannot be checked for lag, and lag is invisible from inside the projection.

co_resident_stores.description: Other stores holding the same or overlapping content -- the duplicate-store census.

trust.description: GRAIN 3 -- whether the resource can be STOOD ON. The PROCESS and ARTIFACT grains describe a resource; only this grain qualifies it. These three are the ones always skipped and the ones that draw blood.

universe.description: What set the resource actually spans.

denominator.description: PRINT IT. 'N of M' with both numbers named. A count without its denominator cannot be judged.

explicitly_out.description: What is KNOWN to be outside. Naming the exclusions is what makes a clean zero readable.

identity_space.description: What key identifies a member, e.g. 'ARN', 'repo path', 'sha1 of anchor node id', 'logical pipeline name'.

x-enum-definitions.stable: The key survives ordinary change to the thing it names.
x-enum-definitions.unstable: The key is derived from something mutable, so the identity dies when that changes and the successor is unlinked.

crosses_spaces.description: Whether this key can be joined to other id spaces WITHOUT a hand-written parse. A concept wearing several id spaces with no declared mapping is the estate's most repeated defect.

declared_mapping.description: Where the cross-space mapping is DECLARED, or null if it is only derivable by convention.

returns_on_failure.description: What the resource actually returns when it CANNOT answer. Exercise it; do not read it from a docstring.

distinguishable_from_true_negative.description: 'no' is the dangerous value: a clean zero that looks identical to a genuine negative. The instrument then reads healthiest exactly when it is most wrong.

silent_degrade_paths.description: Named routes by which the resource can answer confidently from a degraded state.

x-enum-definitions.SOUND: Every row measured; no defect that blocks load-bearing use.
x-enum-definitions.QUALIFIED: Every row measured; defects present, NAMED, and each carrying an owner. Usable within the stated limits.
x-enum-definitions.UNSOUND: A measured defect that blocks load-bearing use until remedied.
x-enum-definitions.INCOMPLETE: One or more rows unmeasured. THIS IS A VERDICT ABOUT THE CARD, NOT ABOUT THE RESOURCE -- the two are routinely collapsed, and collapsing them turns 'we did not finish looking' into 'it is fine'.

x-rule24.domain: standing of one resource as load-bearing substrate, as of this card
x-rule24.intent: gate whether work may be built on this resource
x-rule24.mece: SOUND/QUALIFIED/UNSOUND partition the measured cases; INCOMPLETE covers the unmeasured member and is deliberately about the CARD rather than the resource
x-rule24.state_coherence: INCOMPLETE resolves to one of the other three by measurement; UNSOUND -> QUALIFIED/SOUND requires a REMEDY, not a re-read -- different clocks, which is why the owner column is mandatory

basis.description: How this row's answer was arrived at. A VALUE MUST CARRY ITS CLAIM in a field a consumer can reject on -- never in prose, a name, or the reader's memory of how it was produced.

x-enum-definitions.measured: Read or exercised directly against the thing itself.
x-enum-definitions.inferred: Reasoned from adjacent evidence. NON-ACTIONABLE on its own.
x-enum-definitions.held: Asserted by a named authority without independent measurement here.
x-enum-definitions.absent: No basis exists yet. Honest, and required rather than guessing.

x-rule24.domain: epistemic standing of one card row
x-rule24.intent: let a consumer REFUSE an unmeasured value
x-rule24.mece: measured/inferred/held partition the cases where an answer exists; 'absent' covers the no-answer member
x-rule24.state_coherence: absent -> measured is work; inferred -> measured is re-derivation with a different instrument, never a re-run of the same command

evidence.description: The grounding: 'file:line @ <commit-ish>', a command exercised with its output, or an explicit 'NONE -- basis is inferred/absent'. A line citation without a vintage is not a citation.

owner.description: Serial or role who owns the REMEDY for this row. Rule 24(iv): a stale cache, a missing id grammar and a silent failure mode are three remedies, three owners, three clocks. A card without owners is a wish list. 'UNOWNED' is a legal and loud value.
